concept.name: Volume footprint
concept.definition: A footprint display mode in which each price level inside a bar shows the total volume traded at that level, regardless of side. It reveals the intra-bar volume distribution — which prices attracted business and which were skipped — rather than the buy/sell split.
concept.intuition: It answers 'where inside this bar did the market actually do business?', exposing high-volume shelves and low-volume gaps within a single candle.
concept.mechanics: Tick volume is aggregated per price level per bar and shown as numbers, histograms, or color intensity; the per-bar profile can be read like a miniature volume profile with its own point of control.
concept.failure_modes: Without the bid/ask split it shows where volume occurred but not who initiated it, so it is weaker for reading aggression; accuracy still depends on complete tick data.
concept.misconceptions: High intra-bar volume at a level is not automatically support or resistance — it records where trades happened, and only subsequent price behavior shows whether that level matters.
concept.example: A 15-minute bar shows 60% of its volume concentrated in a three-tick band near its high; the trader marks that band as the bar's high-volume node for the next session.
